meta.title: Exa Search
meta.description: Semantic web search and URL reading through Exa, with multi-key routing and a Billing shortcut.

card.summary: Manage Exa API keys, per-key active state, routing, and a shortcut to Exa Billing. Only active keys are used; the built-in web_search is never replaced.
card.intro: Exa keys are tried in the order shown, and only keys marked Active participate. Priority mode starts with the first active key every time; round-robin starts with the next active key after the previous call's starting key. A 401 or 429 moves that call to the next active key. A 402 marks that key inactive automatically. When every key is inactive, Exa calls return HTTP 402 (payment required). Built-in web_search is unaffected.
card.strategy.title: Key routing
card.strategy.label: Routing strategy
card.strategy.priorityHint: Each call starts with the first active key. Later active keys are fallbacks.
card.strategy.roundRobinHint: Each call starts with the next active key after the previous start, wrapping in list order. Fallbacks continue from there.
card.strategy.failed: Could not save the routing strategy.
card.keys.title: API keys
card.keys.subtitle: Only active keys participate in routing. Click the status tag to enable or disable a key; drag the handle or use the arrow buttons to change the draft order, then save it.
card.keys.empty: No Exa API key is configured yet.
card.keys.addPlaceholder: Paste one or more Exa API keys, separated by commas or new lines
card.keys.addHint: The server trims whitespace, removes empty entries, and ignores keys that are already configured.
card.keys.noNewKeys: No new keys were added; every supplied key is already configured.
card.keys.primaryTitle: Primary — the first active key tried in priority mode
card.keys.activeTitle: Active — included in priority and round-robin routing. Click to disable.
card.keys.inactiveTitle: Inactive — excluded from priority and round-robin routing. Click to enable.
card.keys.allInactive: Every key is inactive. Exa tool calls return HTTP 402 (payment required) until at least one key is enabled. If the keys were disabled by an HTTP 402, add credits first.
card.keys.readOnlyHint: These keys come from the environment that launched dsh. Their key values and order cannot be changed here, but you can still toggle each key's active state. Unset EXA_API_KEYS or EXA_API_KEY in that shell and restart dsh to manage the values.
card.keys.unsavedOrder: Order changes are not saved yet.
card.keys.orderFailed: Could not save the key order.
card.keys.readOnlyReasonPrimary: EXA_API_KEY is supplied read-only by the launching environment.
card.keys.readOnlyReasonList: EXA_API_KEYS is supplied read-only by the launching environment.
card.billing.title: Billing
card.billing.subtitle: Your credit balance, invoices, and auto recharge are managed in the Exa dashboard. A key that returns HTTP 402 is disabled automatically; top up here, then re-enable it above. This card does not read or display your balance.
card.footer: Exa search, advanced search, and fetch are additional tools. Built-in web_search and web_fetch keep their existing providers and schemas.
card.error.readonly_keys: EXA_API_KEYS is supplied read-only by the launching environment. Unset it there and restart dsh, or edit ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml.
card.error.readonly_primary: EXA_API_KEY is supplied read-only by the launching environment. Unset it there and restart dsh.
card.error.key_not_found: That key is no longer configured. Reload the card.
card.error.invalid_order: The order must list every current key exactly once.
card.error.invalid_value: The supplied value is not valid.
